assessments.reasoning: The publisher-governing acquisition came from GNU's official fdl-1.3.txt. Its 22,955-byte body matches the claim's provenance digest. The four verified ranges cover the opening rule, §1 work-notice definition, §2 copying conditions and Addendum. Section 10 in the same body resolves the later-version challenge. The apparent tension between permission to modify a covered work and the prohibition on changing the instrument disappears when each clause is applied to its stated object.

challenge.method: Tested the opening permission against an exact plaintext copy, a copy with the Addendum edited to remove its later-version option, and the license text generated by SPDX. Compared a hypothetical work notice granting 1.3 only with the Addendum example and §10.
challenge.results: The exact copy satisfies the verbatim condition. Editing the Addendum changes the instrument, even if the edit makes its sample resemble the work's actual grant. The SPDX text also differs: its FSF link uses HTTP where the GNU original uses HTTPS, and its lines are reflowed. For the hypothetical work, preserve its authorized 1.3-only notice and feature designations separately alongside the complete publisher text. The Addendum's sample cannot enlarge that grant. Under §10, a distinct authorized later-version clause would allow a choice of 1.3 or a later nondraft version published by the FSF.

limitations: Revision 1 concerns the complete publisher plaintext with SHA-256 110535522396708cea37c72a802c5e7e81391139f5f7985631c93ef242b206a4. It establishes no particular work's grant.
The Addendum is part of the publisher plaintext. Its model notice and the authorized notice accompanying a work serve separate purposes.
reasoning: The FSF's opening permission expressly allows anyone to copy and distribute the complete GNU FDL 1.3 license document verbatim and expressly excludes changes to it. Section 1 gives a different object a defined meaning: a covered Document is a work bearing the copyright holder's licensing notice. Section 2 governs copies of that work. It requires reproduction of the license, copyright notices and applicable work notice, prohibits additional conditions and obstructive technical measures, and refers to further conditions where applicable.
